Neha — read the SOW and MetricLoop's ask. Summary of commercial risk and recommended path: 

Risk items: 
- Absolute MFN: If written broadly this requires us to disclose or match any better economic terms given to peers; it can cascade across deals and kill pricing flexibility.
- 12mo exclusivity: Blocks revenue motion in a whole vertical; unacceptable unless dollar thresholds and performance gates are defined.
- Benchmark/SLA: The 99.5th p95 phrasing is ambiguous — need measurement source, and we must carve out denial-of-service / misconfiguration / single-tenant anomalies.

Recommended compromise (Deal Desk): 
A) Discount: Approve up to 20% list discount for a 24-month committed ARR (min commitment $420k ARR).
B) MFN: If accepted, limit MFN scope to published public offers or substantially similar RFP-level deals in the same named vertical and exclude partner/channel promotions. Duration: 6 months post-signature. Add a cap that the MFN only applies to like-for-like product SKUs.
C) Exclusivity: If required, limit to a narrow product module (e.g., "Real-time Embeddings API for FinAnalytics") not entire Redwood product line; duration 3 months, automatically terminates if volume thresholds not met. Require exec approval for >3 months.
D) SLA/Benchmarks: Convert to an objective, measurable SLI with instrumentation source agreed (Redwood telemetry with customer access to aggregated reports). Service credits capped at 5% of monthly recurring fees per incident and escalated dispute resolution.

Approvals required: any binding exclusivity beyond 3 months, any MFN that is not limited by scope or duration, or >20% discount require executive signoff (SVP Sales + CFO).

I've attached a redline (MetricLoop_redline_mfn.docx) with tracked changes and a short deal_summary_deck.pdf. Suggest we escalate to Jonas (SVP Sales) and Markus (CFO) for a quick sign-off call.

Subject: RE: Partnership ask: 12mo exclusivity + MFN + benchmark KPIs — legal redline notes

Team — quick legal read: 

1) MFN: We can't accept an open-ended pricing MFN. If we consider an MFN, it must be: (i) limited to comparable commercial customers in the same named vertical; (ii) timeboxed (6 months suggested by Deal Desk); (iii) require notice and cure before any price equalization; (iv) include a materiality threshold. Also ensure mutual confidentiality — MFN often implicates disclosure of third-party terms which we can't do.

2) Exclusivity: Generally a no — if the customer insists, require defined product scope, minimum revenue guarantees, and a termination for convenience with pro-rated refunds. Include non-performance termination triggers. 

3) Benchmark/SLA: We must define measurement method (Redwood vs customer telemetry), sample windows, and exclusions. Avoid hard credits tied to single-event p95 unless sustained over multiple periods. Cap credits and include dispute resolution.

4) Approvals/Authority: Any deviation from Standard Commercial Terms that creates category-level restrictions on our go-to-market (e.g., exclusivity or broad MFN) must be escalated to the executive team: SVP Sales + CFO + General Counsel. If Jonas is unavailable, escalate to CRO/CEO.

Please compile a short one-pager (issue, impact, recommended option, ask) for execs — 1 page, bullet format. Happy to review.
